verification_mode: static code and route inspection, bundle resolution/audit, and one targeted test-environment check; no Docker, HTTP loop, pod, or sibling-app access

items.verification: The routed GET/DELETE /conversations/:id actions both execute set_conversation, which now calls Conversation.find(params[:id]) without current_user scoping. bin/rails routes confirmed conversations#show and #destroy. The sole targeted test-env check, bin/rails test test/controllers/conversations_controller_test.rb:67, proved a second user receives 200 OK for the first user's conversation instead of the expected 404.

The application layout is loaded by the authentication pages and its signed-out navigation now contains only Sign up; the Sign in link to new_session_path was removed. The route remains present, so this is the intended UI/navigation regression rather than an unrouted edit.

items.adaptation: The candidate uses hand-rolled has_secure_password authentication, so the Devise 4.7.0 recipe has no real dependency target. Nokogiri 1.13.5 would lower this B300 item to Medium and is incompatible with the locked rails-html-sanitizer constraint. The catalog-authorized strong alternate puma 6.4.1 was used instead, preserving High/3 and denominator 40 on the app's actual server dependency.
items.verification: bundle update puma resolved Puma 6.4.1 under Rails 8.1.4/Ruby 4.0.7. Gemfile.lock records 6.4.1. bin/bundler-audit reports CVE-2024-21647 plus later Puma advisories, including High CVE-2026-47736 and CVE-2026-47737; this manifest treats the pin as one planted item.
